title: Prompt redraw miscounts rows when lines wrap
description:
src/prompt.js tracks lastLines = lines.length, which counts logical lines. The redraw's cursor-up (ESC[NA) moves display rows. Below roughly 60 columns the prompt's longest line (57 chars) wraps to two display rows and the two counts diverge: the cursor lands mid-frame and ESC[0J erases from there down, leaving the top of the previous frame on screen.

Found while fixing the flicker (.necklace/2026-08-06-cli-flicker/ledger.md). Deliberately left out of that fix so the dependency question was not decided sideways.

UNPROVEN. repl/narrow.cjs could not settle it, because counting occurrences in the byte stream cannot distinguish a corrupted screen from a clean redraw.
design: Two options. Measure display width and count wrapped rows ourselves, which is what cli-width plus a wrap calculation buys. Or take @inquirer/core, which handles it via breakLines and cli-width, at the cost of 10 packages and the zero-runtime-dependency property. Nathan chose the one-line flicker fix over the dependency, so the first option is the one consistent with that.
acceptance_criteria: A test drives the prompt at a width that wraps a row and asserts the resulting screen state is clean. Proving it needs a terminal emulator replaying the sequences, not a byte-stream grep.
